title: The Importance of Seeking Forgiveness
summary: The hadith emphasizes the immense joy and blessings Allah grants to those who frequently seek His forgiveness.
translation: Frequent seeking of forgiveness, asking Allah for forgiveness, and crying before Allah is immensely beloved by Him. Engaging in these acts of humility before Allah is greatly favored. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) stated in a hadith that Allah feels immense happiness at the repentance of His servant, likened to a person who, after losing his camel in the wilderness and searching extensively, suddenly finds it. This is how joyful Allah becomes when a servant returns to Him, seeks forgiveness, and pleases Him. Despite being innocent, the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to seek forgiveness more than seventy times a day—some narrations say over a hundred times—to teach the Ummah. The Quran also commands, 'Seek forgiveness from your Lord and then repent to Him.' Thus, frequent seeking of forgiveness is beloved to Allah, and cannot be achieved through neglect. By repeatedly asking for forgiveness, not only are sins erased, but worldly blessings also increase, such as sustenance, offspring, and provisions. Therefore, frequent asking for forgiveness directs Allah’s attention and pleasure toward the person. The Prophet (peace be upon him) mentioned that Allah extends His hand to accept the repentance every night until the sun rises from the west. If this was unimportant to Allah, He would not extend His hand every day and night, awaiting repentance. The Prophet (peace be upon him) also stated that repentance is accepted until the sun rises from the west. Anyone who repents before then will have their repentance accepted by Allah. One should frequently pray to Allah, saying 'Astaghfirullah' many times, from a minimum of 1,200 to a maximum of 12,000 times a day, or whatever feels suitable, to seek His pleasure.
